title: Creatures
build: Thalamus's two-sided disk release, G64 images of side A (SHA-256 4544cf5d…) and side B (b30bb735…) from the C64 Preservation Project's collection; the title says 1990, the collection 1991 (orientation.md)

records.c: The last nine bytes of char_colours (characters $F7-$FF), which this file loads over level 2.1's with the same values. The rest of the world's tiles and character colours ($8009-$86FF) stay as level 2.1 left them.
The addresses of the six map rows, two bytes each: $8715, $87D5, $8895, $8955, $8A15, $8AD5. scroll_column reads them for each new column. The label is the engine's.
map_row_addrs from its second byte: the high byte of row 0's address, and the other rows' (scroll_column reads the high bytes from $870A). The label is the engine's.

Map row 0, the top tile row: one tile number for each map column, 158 columns used of the 192 bytes (the level's length, $9E, at level_end). The row doubles as the column command table: a byte with bit 7 set makes its whole column a command that scroll_column carries out and skips, bit 6 set for the next six sky colours (level_colours_next), clear for the next four band routines (level_band_routines). Command columns: 0 (band routines), 1 (sky colours), 45 (sky colours), 50 (band routines), 132 (sky colours), 140 (band routines). The label is the engine's.

Map row 1 of six, the second tile row (four character rows each): a tile number for each map column, 158 of its 192 bytes drawn; the bytes in command columns are skipped. Its commonest tile is $16. The label is the engine's.

Map row 2 of six, the third tile row (four character rows each): a tile number for each map column, 158 of its 192 bytes drawn; the bytes in command columns are skipped. Its commonest tile is $17. The label is the engine's.

Map row 3 of six, the fourth tile row (four character rows each): a tile number for each map column, 158 of its 192 bytes drawn; the bytes in command columns are skipped. Its commonest tile is $58. The label is the engine's.

Map row 4 of six, the fifth tile row (four character rows each): a tile number for each map column, 158 of its 192 bytes drawn; the bytes in command columns are skipped. Its commonest tile is $26. The label is the engine's.

Map row 5 of six, the bottom tile row (four character rows each): a tile number for each map column, 158 of its 192 bytes drawn; the bytes in command columns are skipped. Its commonest tile is $1F. The label is the engine's.

The level's length in map columns, $9E (158): scroll_column stops scrolling there ($1216) and wakes objects waiting for the end, and game_frame_music starts the end tune and object_kill counts the end creature's death within three columns of it. The label is the engine's.
The first character Clyde and his shots pass through, $38: player_control, its jump and fall, and shot_hits_wall treat every character below it as wall or floor.

Band colours for $D022, the characters' first multicolour (through $12BD-$12C2): six raster bands for each of six changes, which level_colours_next copies six at a time; the raster routines write a band's value at its top unless bit 7 is set, which leaves the colour from the band above. This level reads changes 0, 1, 2 (the others never read): change 0: light blue same same same same orange; change 1: orange same same same same same; change 2: orange same same same same same. The label is the engine's.

Band colours for $D023, the second multicolour (through $12C3-$12C8): six raster bands for each of six changes, which level_colours_next copies six at a time; the raster routines write a band's value at its top unless bit 7 is set, which leaves the colour from the band above. This level reads changes 0, 1, 2 (the others never read): change 0: light red same same same same light green; change 1: light green same light red same same light green; change 2: light green light red same same same light green. The label is the engine's.

Band colours for $D021, the background (through $12C9-$12CE): six raster bands for each of six changes, which level_colours_next copies six at a time; the raster routines write a band's value at its top unless bit 7 is set, which leaves the colour from the band above. This level reads changes 0, 1, 2 (the others never read): change 0: brown same same same same same; change 1: brown same same same same same; change 2: brown same same same same same. The label is the engine's.

The band table: four entries per change of band routines, for bands 2-5, each an index into the engine's routine table at $12CF (level_band_routines). This level reads groups 0, 1, 2 (the others never read): 0: 0 1 0 2; 1: 1 0 2 0; 2: 0 2 0 0. The label is the engine's.

The last scroll position of each section: level_section_from_scroll picks the first entry not below the scroll position as the section Clyde restarts in after losing a life: $25 $48 $69 $78 $FF $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.

The scroll position (the map column at the right edge) each section restarts from, which get_ready writes to $1273; $FF for the first means from the start: $FF $1F $41 $62 $7E $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.

The scroll position at which each section's opening run ends and play begins (stage_start writes it into stage_intro_loop's compare at $1A72): $0C $2A $4C $6D $8A $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.

How many map columns the Get Ready screen's landscape strip runs for in each section (get_ready_strip's compare at $3AFE): $27 $36 $56 $77 $92 $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.
The strip's scroll speed for each section (the SBC operand at $3AEA): $02 $03 $04 $05 $07 $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.

The x of the Get Ready screen's marker over the landscape strip in each section: raster_ready_marker places three sprites showing block 13 a pixel apart from this x (its LDX operand at $394F); block 13 stays blank until the strip has stopped, when the Get Ready raster code draws a small pattern into it from ready_columns_1: $28 $B0 $B0 $B0 $B0 $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.
The marker's y in each section (raster_ready_marker's LDA operand at $395E): $8B $92 $9A $A2 $9A $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.

The read position in the sky colour tables when a section starts: get_ready copies the six colours from there: $00 $00 $06 $06 $0C $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.
Where the sky colour tables are read from after a section starts, for the next colour command: $00 $06 $06 $0C $0C $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.

The read position in band_table for each section's start; get_ready reads four entries from it (for a first section's $FC the read runs past band_table into strip_tile_colours and wraps to 0, and the command in map column 0 then sets the bands): $FC $00 $04 $04 $04 $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.
Clyde's starting x in each section (into stage_main_setup's LDA at $1A9B): $37 $77 $6E $6A $4B $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.
Clyde's starting y in each section (into the LDA at $1AA0): $44 $5D $7D $9D $7D $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.
The low byte of the first spawn record of each section (get_ready into $1FC3): $9000, $91CB, $9352, $94C8, $95D8, $9000; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.
The high byte of each section's first spawn record (into $1FC4): $90 $91 $93 $94 $95 $90; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.

The scrolling, in pixels, before each section's first record is read (into the spawn counter $1FC2): $00 $08 $09 $81 $5F $00; the level has 5 sections, so entry 5 is never read. The label is the engine's.
print_big's string 1, the stage's name on the Get Ready screen: "STAGE 2.2" and $FF. The label is the engine's.
print_at's string 0, the Get Ready screen's first line, centred in 40 characters: "PIRANHA PONDS LEADING TO" and $FF. The label is the engine's.
print_at's string 3, the Get Ready screen's second line: "THE BLACK FOREST OF GATEAU" and $FF. The label is the engine's.

The colours of the Get Ready screen's three potion-creature icons, four sets of three: raster_ready_icons shows the last set first, then steps through the first three every ten frames. green white light blue; green light red white; white light red light blue; green light red light blue. The label is the engine's.
The stage's time limit, three digits: 600. timer_reset copies them to the panel's timer. The label is the engine's.

The level's five hook addresses, copied by level_begin into the engine's calls: $A8C3 every frame (level_frame_call), $A334 for Clyde (level_player_call), $A36C for his jump (level_jump_call), $A3C6 for his animation (level_anim_call) and $A3FD in place of firing (level_hook_call). The label is the engine's.
level_hooks' second address, the player routine. The label is the engine's.
level_hooks' third address, the jump routine. The label is the engine's.
level_hooks' fourth address, the animation routine. The label is the engine's.
level_hooks' fifth address, called instead of player_fire. The label is the engine's.
The Get Ready strip's colours, read by raster_ready_strip: brown, orange (the two multicolour registers) and, at $8CF4, black for the background. The label is the engine's.
strip_colours' second byte. The label is the engine's.
strip_colours' third byte, the strip's background. The label is the engine's.
The colour of each tile on the Get Ready strip, 96 bytes: get_ready_strip draws each map byte as a single character, the miniature of its tile, in this colour. The label is the engine's.
The Get Ready screen's backdrop character, $1F, which get_ready fills the strip's six rows with. The label is the engine's.
The address of the level's tune, $9C30, played from the start of play when the music option is on (stage_main_setup). The label is the engine's.
tune_addr's high byte. The label is the engine's.
The address of the end tune, $A9C6, which game_frame_music starts within three columns of the level's end. The label is the engine's.
end_tune_addr's high byte. The label is the engine's.
The low bytes of the 56 object types' animation scripts; object_set_type and object_spawn read them with anim_hi. The label is the engine's.
The high bytes of the object types' animation scripts. The label is the engine's.
Each object type's animation speed: a new byte of its script every speed + 1 of the object's turns (each object animates every other frame); $7F all but stops it. The label is the engine's.
The low bytes of the 15 colour cycles' lists, chosen by a spawn record's colour byte ($10-$1E) or a death's colour cycle. The label is the engine's.
The high bytes of the colour cycles' lists. The label is the engine's.
Each colour cycle's speed: frames between its colours (obj_cycle_speed). The label is the engine's.
The low bytes of the 32 x movement scripts, named by a spawn record (byte 1, and byte 0's high nibble at death). The label is the engine's.
The high bytes of the x movement scripts. The label is the engine's.
The low bytes of the 32 y movement scripts (record byte 2, and byte 10's high nibble at death). The label is the engine's.
The high bytes of the y movement scripts. The label is the engine's.
Hit points by the low nibble of record byte 9: $FF $00 $01 $02 $03 $05 $07 $09 $13 $27 $45 $63 $2C $AE $1A $FE ($FF: shots never harm it, they only make it flash). The label is the engine's.

Wake delays by the high nibble of record byte 9: an object with 0 is awake at once; any other value leaves it asleep (obj_awake clear: it neither moves nor animates, and cannot be hit) while objects_scroll counts the value down once a frame, waking it when the count passes zero, except that $FE waits for the level's end, when scroll_column wakes it, and $FF for ever: $00 $40 $20 $80 $C0 $29 $15 $70 $04 $03 $6C $02 $86 $FE $01 $FF. The label is the engine's.
Start delays, in frames, by the top two bits of record bytes 1 and 2 together: $00 $10 $60 $70 $80 $20 $40 $00 $00 $00 $00 $00 $00 $00 $00 $00. The label is the engine's.
Hits needed before an object's hit response runs, by the low nibble of record byte 15: $00 $01 $02 $04 $06 $09 $0F $10 $20 $40 $00 $00 $00 $00 $00 $FF. The label is the engine's.

The low bytes of six message addresses the witch's shop reads from the loaded level ($EB01-$EB65 in the shop's code), high bytes at shop_text_hi: 0 $990B, 1 $8F4A, 2 $98CA, 3 $994A, 4 $994A, 5 $98A9, the same as level 2.1's. The shop greets Clyde with message 0 when his lives count ($B7BF) is 0, 2 when it is below shop_lives_mark, 1 otherwise; it shows message 3 as its second line and message 5 as the third clue. Nothing reads message 4.
The high bytes of the six shop messages' addresses (see shop_text_lo).
3 (level 2.1 has 7): with a lives count below this (but not 0) the witch's shop greets Clyde with shop_text 2, "YOU BETTER BE MORE CAREFUL"; with this many or more, with shop_text 1.
The x offsets a riding object can take from the object carrying it (ride_parent, by the low nibble of record byte 14): 0 2 4 6 8 10 12 14. The label is the engine's.
The y offsets for a riding object (bits 4-6 of record byte 14): 0 3 6 9 12 15 18 26.
The slot of the level's end creature, 2: killing it within three columns of the level's end starts the stage-complete countdown (object_kill). The label is the engine's.

"USE THE SWITCH" $FF "TO CHANGE THE" $FF "DIRECTION OF THE" $FF "CONVEYOR BELT." $00: the first clue the witch's shop sells for torture chamber 2, the saw mill, as in level 2.1's file. The shop takes it from this fixed address in every level.
"HI THERE MY CUTE" / "BUNDLE OF FLUFF." / "I'M GLAD YOU'RE" / "DOING WELL." ($FF between lines, $00 at the end): shop_text 1, the witch's greeting when Clyde has shop_lives_mark lives or more.

"SLEEPY EARTH" / "CREATURES MUST BE" / "WOKEN UP." ($FF between lines, $00 at the end): the witch's shop takes its second clue from this fixed address on stages 1-6 ($9908 from stage 7).
